Response Text:---
The ConsolePlayer class is designed to allow a human player to input moves via the console, validating and parsing their input into valid Move objects. The main method to implement is nextMove, which prompts the user, reads input, validates it, and ensures the move is among available moves.

Here's a complete implementation of the ConsolePlayer class with the TODO completed:

```java
package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.Scanner;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
    private final Scanner scanner;

    public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
        super(name, color);
        this.scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    }

    public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
        this(name, Color.GREEN);
    }

    /**
     * Choose a move from available moves.
     * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
     * player's turn.
     * <p>
     * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
     * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
     * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
     * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
     * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
     * <p>
     * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
     * facilitate programming.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        while (true) {
            System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3):");
            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please enter move in format 'a1->b3'.");
                continue;
            }

            // Validate the move against available moves
            boolean isValid = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValid = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValid) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please choose a valid move from the list.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optional: validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new assignment.protocol.rules.Rule[] {
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OccupiedRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.VacantRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.NilMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.ArcherMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            char xChar = str.charAt(0);
            if (xChar < 'a' || xChar > 'z') {
                return null;
            }
            int x = xChar - 'a';

            String yStr = str.substring(1);
            int y = Integer.parseInt(yStr) - 1;
            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        String[] segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;
        }
        Place source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
        if (source == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
        if (destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }
}
```

            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please enter move in format 'a1->b3'.");
                continue;
            }

            // Validate the move against available moves
            boolean isValid = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValid = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValid) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please choose a valid move from the list.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optional: validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new assignment.protocol.rules.Rule[] {
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OccupiedRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.VacantRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.NilMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.ArcherMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            char xChar = str.charAt(0);
            if (xChar < 'a' || xChar > 'z') {
                return null;
            }
            int x = xChar - 'a';

            String yStr = str.substring(1);
            int y = Integer.parseInt(yStr) - 1;
            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        String[] segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;
        }
        Place source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
        if (source == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
        if (destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }
}

     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
     * facilitate programming.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        while (true) {
            System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3):");
            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please enter move in format 'a1->b3'.");
                continue;
            }

            // Validate the move against available moves
            boolean isValid = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValid = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValid) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please choose a valid move from the list.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optional: validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new assignment.protocol.rules.Rule[] {
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OccupiedRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.VacantRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.NilMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.ArcherMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            char xChar = str.charAt(0);
            if (xChar < 'a' || xChar > 'z') {
                return null;
            }
            int x = xChar - 'a';

            String yStr = str.substring(1);
            int y = Integer.parseInt(yStr) - 1;
            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        String[] segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;
        }
        Place source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
        if (source == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
        if (destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }

	 * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.

	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
	 * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
	 * facilitate programming.
	 * This is VERY different from the coordinate used in console display.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game           the current game object
	 * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
	 * @return the chosen move
	 */
	@Override
	public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return availableMoves[0];
	}

	private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(),
				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return rule.getDescription();
			}

			var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
			if (piece == null) {
				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
			}
			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

	private static Move parseMove(String str) {
		var segments = str.split("->");
		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}
		return new Move(source, destination);
	}
}

package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.Scanner;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
    private final Scanner scanner;

    public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
        super(name, color);
        this.scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    }

    public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
        this(name, Color.GREEN);
    }

    /**
     * Choose a move from available moves.
     * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
     * player's turn.
     * <p>
     * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
     * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
     * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
     * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
     * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
     * <p>
     * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
     * facilitate programming.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        while (true) {
            System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3):");
            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please enter move in format 'a1->b3'.");
                continue;
            }

            // Validate the move against available moves
            boolean isValid = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValid = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValid) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please choose a valid move from the list.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optional: validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        var rules = new assignment.protocol.rules.Rule[] {
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.OccupiedRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.VacantRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.NilMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.ArcherMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightMoveRule(),
            new assignment.protocol.rules.KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {
            char xChar = str.charAt(0);
            if (xChar < 'a' || xChar > 'z') {
                return null;
            }
            int x = xChar - 'a';

            String yStr = str.substring(1);
            int y = Integer.parseInt(yStr) - 1;
            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Move parseMove(String str) {
        String[] segments = str.split("->");
        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;
        }
        Place source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
        if (source == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
        if (destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }
}

```java
package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;

import assignment.protocol.Player;
```

```java
import assignment.protocol.rules.Rule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.OutOfBoundaryRule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.OccupiedRule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.VacantRule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.NilMoveRule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.FirstNMovesProtectionRule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.ArcherMoveRule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.KnightMoveRule;
import assignment.protocol.rules.KnightBlockRule;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
    private final Scanner scanner;

    public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
        super(name, color);
        this.scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    }

    public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
        this(name, Color.GREEN);
    }

    /**
     * Choose a move from available moves.
     * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
     * player's turn.
     * <p>
     * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
     * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
     * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
     * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
     * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
     * <p>
     * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
     * facilitate programming.</strong>
     *
     * @param game           the current game object
     * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
     * @return the chosen move
     */
    @Override
    public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
        while (true) {
            System.out.println("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3):");
            String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();

            Move move = parseMove(input);
            if (move == null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid format. Please enter move in format 'a1->b3'.");
                continue;
            }

            // Validate the move against available moves
            boolean isValid = false;
            for (Move m : availableMoves) {
                if (m.equals(move)) {
                    isValid = true;
                    move = m; // Use the actual move object from availableMoves
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!isValid) {
                System.out.println("Move not available. Please choose a valid move from the list.");
                continue;
            }

            // Optional: validate move with game rules
            String validationError = validateMove(game, move);
            if (validationError != null) {
                System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);
                continue;
            }

            return move;
        }
    }

    private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
        Rule[] rules = new Rule[] {
            new OutOfBoundaryRule(),
            new OccupiedRule(),
            new VacantRule(),
            new NilMoveRule(),
            new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()),
            new ArcherMoveRule(),
            new KnightMoveRule(),
            new KnightBlockRule()
        };
        for (var rule : rules) {
            if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
                return rule.getDescription();
            }
        }
        var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
        if (piece == null) {
            return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
        }
        if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
            return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
        if (str.length() < 2) {
            return null;
        }
        try {

            if (xChar < 'a' || xChar > 'z') {
                return null;

            int y = Integer.parseInt(yStr) - 1;
            return new Place(x, y);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }

        if (segments.length != 2) {
            return null;

        if (source == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Place destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
        if (destination == null) {
            return null;
        }
        return new Move(source, destination);
    }
```

	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull

		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();

				break;

		}

	 * @param direction The direction to offset.

	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.

	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

The class `GameBoardController` manages high-level operations on a `GameBoard`, such as moving the player, undoing moves, and simulating moves. Below is a complete implementation of the class with all TODOs addressed, assuming typical behavior for such a game controller.

**Key assumptions:**
- `GameBoard` has methods like `getCell(Position)`, `setCell(Position, Cell)`, `getPlayerPosition()`, `setPlayerPosition(Position)`, and `clone()` for state management.
- `MoveResult` has subclasses `Valid` (with `Alive` and `Dead`) and `Invalid`.
- `Position` has methods like `offsetByOrNull()`, `equals()`, and proper constructors.
- `Direction` provides `getOffset()` returning a `Position` delta.
- The game state can be cloned or saved/restored for undo functionality.

**Complete class implementation:**

```java
package pa1.controller;

import pa1.model.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Controller for {@link GameBoard}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class is responsible for providing high-level operations to mutate a {@link GameBoard}. This should be the only
 * class which mutates the game board; Other classes should use this class to mutate the game board.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameBoardController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    // To support undo, store the previous state of the game board
    private GameBoard previousState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameBoard The instance of {@link GameBoard} to control.
     */
    public GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
        // Save initial state for potential undo
        this.previousState = gameBoard.clone();
    }

    /**
     * Moves the player in the given direction.
     *
     * <p>
     * You should ensure that the game board is only mutated if the move is valid and results in the player still being
     * alive. If the player dies after moving or the move is invalid, the game board should remain in the same state as
     * before this method was called.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.
     */
    public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
        // Save current state for undo
        previousState = gameBoard.clone();

        Position currentPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
        MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPos, direction);

        if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
            // Move is valid and player is alive
            // Save previous state before mutation
            previousState = gameBoard.clone();

            // Update the game board: move player
            gameBoard.setCell(currentPos, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
            gameBoard.setCell(validMove.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

            // Remove collected gems and extra lives from the board
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveMove) {
                for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
                }
                for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
                }
            }

            // Check if the move resulted in death
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
                // Player died, revert to previous state
                gameBoard = previousState;
            }

            return validMove;
        } else {
            // Invalid move, do not change the game board
            return moveResult;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
     */
    public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
        if (prevMove == null) {
            return;
        }
        // Revert to previous state
        this.gameBoard = previousState.clone();

        // Restore player position
        if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid valid) {
            gameBoard.setCell(valid.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
            // Restore collected gems and extra lives if needed
            // (Assuming the game board's state is restored entirely, so no need to manually restore collected items)
        }
    }

    /**
     * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
     *
     * <p>
     * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
     * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param position  The original position of the player.
     * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
     * moving.
     */
    @NotNull
    private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
        final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
        Position lastValidPosition = position;

        do {
            final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
            if (newPosition == null) {
                break;
            }

            lastValidPosition = newPosition;

            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);
            if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
                break;
            }

                    return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
                }

                    collectedGems.add(newPosition);
                } else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
                }
            }
        } while (true);

        if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
            return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
        }

        return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
    }

    /**
     * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
     *
     * @param position  The original position.
     * @param direction The direction to offset.
     * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
     * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
     */
    @Nullable
    private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
                gameBoard.getNumCols());

        if (newPos == null) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
            return null;
        }

        return newPos;
    }
}
```

**Notes:**
- The constructor saves the initial state for undo purposes.
- `makeMove` attempts to move the player, updates the game board if valid, and handles death.
- `undoMove` restores the previous game state.
- The `tryMove` method simulates movement without mutating the game state.
- The code assumes the existence of `clone()` methods and proper implementations of `Position`, `Cell`, `EntityCell`, and game entities.

This implementation ensures the game logic is encapsulated and adheres to the specified behavior.

public class GameBoardController {

    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    private GameBoard previousState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.

     * @param gameBoard The instance of {@link GameBoard} to control.

        // Save initial state for potential undo
        this.previousState = gameBoard.clone();

    /**
     * Moves the player in the given direction.
     *
     * <p>
     * You should ensure that the game board is only mutated if the move is valid and results in the player still being
     * alive. If the player dies after moving or the move is invalid, the game board should remain in the same state as
     * before this method was called.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.
     */

            previousState = gameBoard.clone();

            // Update the game board: move player
            gameBoard.setCell(currentPos, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
            gameBoard.setCell(validMove.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

                    gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());

                    gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
                }

                gameBoard = previousState;
            }

            return validMove;
        } else {

            return moveResult;
        }
    }

    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    // To support undo, store the previous state of the game board
    private GameBoard previousState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameBoard The instance of {@link GameBoard} to control.
     */
    public GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
        // Save initial state for potential undo
        this.previousState = gameBoard.clone();
    }

    /**
     * Moves the player in the given direction.
     *
     * <p>
     * You should ensure that the game board is only mutated if the move is valid and results in the player still being
     * alive. If the player dies after moving or the move is invalid, the game board should remain in the same state as
     * before this method was called.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.
     */
    public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
        // Save current state for undo
        previousState = gameBoard.clone();

        Position currentPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
        MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPos, direction);

        if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
            // Move is valid and player is alive
            // Save previous state before mutation
            previousState = gameBoard.clone();

            // Update the game board: move player
            gameBoard.setCell(currentPos, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
            gameBoard.setCell(validMove.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

            // Remove collected gems and extra lives from the board
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveMove) {
                for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
                }
                for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
                }
            }

            // Check if the move resulted in death
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
                // Player died, revert to previous state
                gameBoard = previousState;
            }

            return validMove;
        } else {
            // Invalid move, do not change the game board
            return moveResult;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
     */
    public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
        if (prevMove == null) {
            return;
        }
        // Revert to previous state
        this.gameBoard = previousState.clone();

        // Restore player position
        if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid valid) {
            gameBoard.setCell(valid.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
            // Restore collected gems and extra lives if needed
            // (Assuming the game board's state is restored entirely, so no need to manually restore collected items)
        }
    }

    /**
     * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
     *
     * <p>
     * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
     * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param position  The original position of the player.
     * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
     * moving.
     */
    @NotNull
    private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
        final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
        Position lastValidPosition = position;

        do {
            final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
            if (newPosition == null) {
                break;
            }

            lastValidPosition = newPosition;

            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);
            if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
                break;
            }

            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
                    return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
                }

                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    collectedGems.add(newPosition);
                } else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
                }
            }
        } while (true);

        if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
            return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
        }

        return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
    }

    /**
     * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
     *
     * @param position  The original position.
     * @param direction The direction to offset.
     * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
     * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
     */
    @Nullable
    private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
                gameBoard.getNumCols());

        if (newPos == null) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
            return null;
        }

        return newPos;
    }
}

package pa1.controller;

import pa1.model.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Controller for {@link GameBoard}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class is responsible for providing high-level operations to mutate a {@link GameBoard}. This should be the only
 * class which mutates the game board; Other classes should use this class to mutate the game board.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameBoardController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    // To support undo, store the previous state of the game board
    private GameBoard previousState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameBoard The instance of {@link GameBoard} to control.
     */
    public GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
        // Save initial state for potential undo
        this.previousState = gameBoard.clone();
    }

    /**
     * Moves the player in the given direction.
     *
     * <p>
     * You should ensure that the game board is only mutated if the move is valid and results in the player still being
     * alive. If the player dies after moving or the move is invalid, the game board should remain in the same state as
     * before this method was called.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.
     */
    public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
        // Save current state for undo
        previousState = gameBoard.clone();

        Position currentPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
        MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPos, direction);

        if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
            // Move is valid and player is alive
            // Save previous state before mutation
            previousState = gameBoard.clone();

            // Update the game board: move player
            gameBoard.setCell(currentPos, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
            gameBoard.setCell(validMove.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

            // Remove collected gems and extra lives from the board
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveMove) {
                for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
                }
                for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
                }
            }

            // Check if the move resulted in death
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
                // Player died, revert to previous state
                gameBoard = previousState;
            }

            return validMove;
        } else {
            // Invalid move, do not change the game board
            return moveResult;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
     */
    public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
        if (prevMove == null) {
            return;
        }
        // Revert to previous state
        this.gameBoard = previousState.clone();

        // Restore player position
        if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid valid) {
            gameBoard.setCell(valid.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
            // Restore collected gems and extra lives if needed
            // (Assuming the game board's state is restored entirely, so no need to manually restore collected items)
        }
    }

    /**
     * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
     *
     * <p>
     * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
     * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param position  The original position of the player.
     * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
     * moving.
     */
    @NotNull
    private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
        final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
        Position lastValidPosition = position;

        do {
            final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
            if (newPosition == null) {
                break;
            }

            lastValidPosition = newPosition;

            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);
            if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
                break;
            }

            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
                    return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
                }

                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    collectedGems.add(newPosition);
                } else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
                }
            }
        } while (true);

        if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
            return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
        }

        return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
    }

    /**
     * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
     *
     * @param position  The original position.
     * @param direction The direction to offset.
     * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
     * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
     */
    @Nullable
    private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
                gameBoard.getNumCols());

        if (newPos == null) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
            return null;
        }

        return newPos;
    }

```java
package pa1.controller;

import pa1.model.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Controller for {@link GameBoard}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class is responsible for providing high-level operations to mutate a {@link GameBoard}. This should be the only
 * class which mutates the game board; Other classes should use this class to mutate the game board.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameBoardController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    // To support undo, store the previous state of the game board
    private GameBoard previousState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameBoard The instance of {@link GameBoard} to control.
     */
    public GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
        // Save initial state for potential undo
```
```java
        this.previousState = cloneGameBoard(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /**
     * Moves the player in the given direction.
     *
     * <p>
     * You should ensure that the game board is only mutated if the move is valid and results in the player still being
     * alive. If the player dies after moving or the move is invalid, the game board should remain in the same state as
     * before this method was called.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.
     */
    public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
        // Save current state for undo
        previousState = cloneGameBoard(this.gameBoard);

        Position currentPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
        MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPos, direction);

        if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
            // Move is valid and player is alive
            // Save previous state before mutation
            previousState = cloneGameBoard(this.gameBoard);

            // Update the game board: move player
            gameBoard.setCell(currentPos, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
            gameBoard.setCell(validMove.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

            // Remove collected gems and extra lives from the board
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveMove) {
                for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
                }
                for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
                }
            }

            // Check if the move resulted in death
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
                // Player died, revert to previous state
                this.gameBoard.copyFrom(previousState);
            }

            return validMove;
        } else {
            // Invalid move, do not change the game board
            return moveResult;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
     */
    public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
        if (prevMove == null) {
            return;
        }
        // Revert to previous state
        this.gameBoard.copyFrom(previousState);

        // Restore player position
        if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid valid) {
            gameBoard.setCell(valid.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
            // Restoring collected items is handled by copying the entire game board state
        }
    }

    /**
     * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
     *
     * <p>
     * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
     * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param position  The original position of the player.
     * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
     * moving.
     */
    @NotNull
    private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
        final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
        Position lastValidPosition = position;

        do {
            final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
            if (newPosition == null) {
                break;
            }

            lastValidPosition = newPosition;

            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);
            if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
                break;
            }

            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
                    return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
                }

                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    collectedGems.add(newPosition);
                } else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
                }
            }
        } while (true);

        if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
            return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
        }

        return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
    }

    /**
     * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
     *
     * @param position  The original position.
     * @param direction The direction to offset.
     * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
     * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
     */
    @Nullable
    private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
                gameBoard.getNumCols());

        if (newPos == null) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
            return null;
        }

        return newPos;
    }

    /**
     * Helper method to clone a GameBoard.
     */
    private GameBoard cloneGameBoard(@NotNull GameBoard original) {
        // Assuming GameBoard has a public clone method
        if (original instanceof Cloneable) {
            try {
                return (GameBoard) original.getClass().getMethod("clone").invoke(original);
            } catch (Exception e) {
                throw new RuntimeException("Failed to clone GameBoard", e);
            }
        } else {
            throw new UnsupportedOperationException("GameBoard must implement clone()");
        }
    }
}
```

package pa1.controller;

import pa1.model.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Controller for {@link GameBoard}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class is responsible for providing high-level operations to mutate a {@link GameBoard}. This should be the only
 * class which mutates the game board; Other classes should use this class to mutate the game board.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameBoardController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    // To support undo, store the previous state of the game board
    private GameBoard previousState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameBoard The instance of {@link GameBoard} to control.
     */
    public GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
        // Save initial state for potential undo
        this.previousState = gameBoard.clone();
    }

    /**
     * Moves the player in the given direction.
     *
     * <p>
     * You should ensure that the game board is only mutated if the move is valid and results in the player still being
     * alive. If the player dies after moving or the move is invalid, the game board should remain in the same state as
     * before this method was called.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.
     */
    public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
        // Save current state for undo
        previousState = gameBoard.clone();

        Position currentPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
        MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPos, direction);

        if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
            // Move is valid and player is alive
            // Save previous state before mutation
            previousState = gameBoard.clone();

            // Update the game board: move player
            gameBoard.setCell(currentPos, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
            gameBoard.setCell(validMove.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

            // Remove collected gems and extra lives from the board
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveMove) {
                for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
                }
                for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
                }
            }

            // Check if the move resulted in death
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
                // Player died, revert to previous state
                gameBoard = previousState;
            }

            return validMove;
        } else {
            // Invalid move, do not change the game board
            return moveResult;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
     */
    public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
        if (prevMove == null) {
            return;
        }
        // Revert to previous state
        this.gameBoard = previousState.clone();

        // Restore player position
        if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid valid) {
            gameBoard.setCell(valid.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
            // Restore collected gems and extra lives if needed
            // (Assuming the game board's state is restored entirely, so no need to manually restore collected items)
        }
    }

    /**
     * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
     *
     * <p>
     * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
     * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param position  The original position of the player.
     * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
     * moving.
     */
    @NotNull
    private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
        final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
        Position lastValidPosition = position;

        do {
            final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
            if (newPosition == null) {
                break;
            }

            lastValidPosition = newPosition;

            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);
            if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
                break;
            }

            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
                    return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
                }

                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    collectedGems.add(newPosition);
                } else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
                }
            }
        } while (true);

        if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
            return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
        }

        return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
    }

    /**
     * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
     *
     * @param position  The original position.
     * @param direction The direction to offset.
     * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
     * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
     */
    @Nullable
    private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
                gameBoard.getNumCols());

        if (newPos == null) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
            return null;
        }

        return newPos;
    }

        final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
        final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
        Position lastValidPosition = position;

        do {
            final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
            if (newPosition == null) {
                break;
            }

            lastValidPosition = newPosition;

            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);
            if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
                break;
            }

            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
                    return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
                }

                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    collectedGems.add(newPosition);
                } else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
                }
            }
        } while (true);

        if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
            return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
        }

        return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
    }

    /**
     * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
     *
     * @param position  The original position.
     * @param direction The direction to offset.
     * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
     * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
     */
    @Nullable
    private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
                gameBoard.getNumCols());

        if (newPos == null) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
            return null;
        }

        return newPos;
    }

    /**
     * Helper method to clone a GameBoard.
     */
    private GameBoard cloneGameBoard(@NotNull GameBoard original) {
        // Assuming GameBoard has a public clone method
        if (original instanceof Cloneable) {
            try {
                return (GameBoard) original.getClass().getMethod("clone").invoke(original);
            } catch (Exception e) {
                throw new RuntimeException("Failed to clone GameBoard", e);
            }
        } else {
            throw new UnsupportedOperationException("GameBoard must implement clone()");
        }
    }

```java
package pa1.controller;

import pa1.model.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Controller for {@link GameBoard}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class is responsible for providing high-level operations to mutate a {@link GameBoard}. This should be the only
 * class which mutates the game board; Other classes should use this class to mutate the game board.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameBoardController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    // To support undo, store the previous state of the game board
    private GameBoard previousState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameBoard The instance of {@link GameBoard} to control.
     */
    public GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
        // Save initial state for potential undo
        this.previousState = cloneGameBoard(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /**
     * Moves the player in the given direction.
     *
     * <p>
     * You should ensure that the game board is only mutated if the move is valid and results in the player still being
     * alive. If the player dies after moving or the move is invalid, the game board should remain in the same state as
     * before this method was called.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param direction Direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the result of this action.
     */
    public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
        // Save current state for undo
        previousState = cloneGameBoard(this.gameBoard);

        Position currentPos = gameBoard.getPlayerPosition();
        MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(currentPos, direction);

        if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
            // Move is valid and player is alive
            // Save previous state before mutation
            previousState = cloneGameBoard(this.gameBoard);

            // Update the game board: move player
            gameBoard.setCell(currentPos, new EmptyCell()); // Clear old position
            gameBoard.setCell(validMove.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell()); // Set new position

            // Remove collected gems and extra lives from the board
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveMove) {
                for (Position gemPos : aliveMove.getCollectedGems()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EmptyCell());
                }
                for (Position lifePos : aliveMove.getCollectedExtraLives()) {
                    gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EmptyCell());
                }
            }

            // Check if the move resulted in death
            if (validMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead) {
                // Player died, revert to previous state
                this.gameBoard.copyFrom(previousState);
            }

            return validMove;
        } else {
            // Invalid move, do not change the game board
            return moveResult;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
     */
    public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
        if (prevMove == null) {
            return;
        }
        // Revert to previous state
        this.gameBoard.copyFrom(previousState);

        // Restore player position
        if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid valid) {
            gameBoard.setCell(valid.getNewPosition(), new PlayerCell());
            // Restoring collected items is handled by copying the entire game board state
        }
    }

    /**
     * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
     *
     * <p>
     * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
     * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param position  The original position of the player.
     * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
     * moving.
     */
    @NotNull
    private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
        final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
        Position lastValidPosition = position;

        do {
            final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
            if (newPosition == null) {
                break;
            }

            lastValidPosition = newPosition;

            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(newPosition);
            if (cell instanceof StopCell) {
                break;
            }

            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
                    return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
                }

                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    collectedGems.add(newPosition);
                } else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
                    collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
                }
            }
        } while (true);

        if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
            return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
        }

        return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
    }

    /**
     * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
     *
     * @param position  The original position.
     * @param direction The direction to offset.
     * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
     * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
     */
    @Nullable
    private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position);
        Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

        final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
                gameBoard.getNumCols());

        if (newPos == null) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
            return null;
        }

        return newPos;
    }

    /**
     * Helper method to clone a GameBoard.
     */
    private GameBoard cloneGameBoard(@NotNull GameBoard original) {
        // Assuming GameBoard has a public clone() method
        try {
            return (GameBoard) original.getClass().getMethod("clone").invoke(original);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Failed to clone GameBoard", e);
        }
    }
```

Response Text:---
The `GameController` class manages the game state for `pa1.InertiaTextGame`. It should initialize the `gameState` in the constructor, process moves by updating the game state accordingly, and handle undo actions by reverting to previous states.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
package pa1.controller;

import pa1.model.Direction;
import pa1.model.GameState;
import pa1.model.MoveResult;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Controller for {@link pa1.InertiaTextGame}.
 *
 * <p>
 * All game state mutations should be performed by this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameState gameState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameState The instance of {@link GameState} to control.
     */
    public GameController(final GameState gameState) {
        // Initialize the gameState with a non-null value
        this.gameState = Objects.requireNonNull(gameState, "gameState cannot be null");
    }

    /**
     * Processes a Move action performed by the player.
     *
     * @param direction The direction the player wants to move to.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} indicating the result of the action.
     */
    public MoveResult processMove(final Direction direction) {
        // Save current state for undo
        gameState.saveState();

        // Attempt to move in the specified direction
        boolean moved = gameState.move(direction);

        if (moved) {
            // Return a successful move result
            return new MoveResult(true, "Moved " + direction);
        } else {
            // If move failed, revert to previous state
            gameState.undo();
            return new MoveResult(false, "Cannot move " + direction);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Processes an Undo action performed by the player.
     *
     * @return {@code false} if there are no steps to undo.
     */
    public boolean processUndo() {
        // Check if undo is possible
        if (gameState.canUndo()) {
            gameState.undo();
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**

- The constructor uses `Objects.requireNonNull` to ensure `gameState` is not null.
- `processMove` saves the current state before attempting to move. If the move is successful, it returns a positive `MoveResult`; otherwise, it reverts the state and indicates failure.
- `processUndo` checks if undo is possible via `gameState.canUndo()`, performs undo if possible, and returns whether the undo was successful.

This implementation assumes that `GameState` has methods like `saveState()`, `move(Direction)`, `undo()`, and `canUndo()`, which are typical for managing game state history.

import pa1.model.Direction;

/**

    public MoveResult processMove(final Direction direction) {

 * <p>
 * All game state mutations should be performed by this class.
 * </p>

public class GameController {

    @NotNull
    private final GameState gameState;

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     *
     * @param gameState The instance of {@link GameState} to control.
     */
    public GameController(final GameState gameState) {
```java
        this.gameState = java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(gameState, "gameState cannot be null");
    }

    /**
     * Processes a Move action performed by the player.
     *
     * @param direction The direction the player wants to move to.
     * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} indicating the result of the action.
     */
    public MoveResult processMove(final Direction direction) {
```
        // Save current state for undo
        gameState.saveState();

        // Attempt to move in the specified direction
        boolean moved = gameState.tryMove(direction);

        if (moved) {
            // Return a successful move result
            return new MoveResult(true, "Moved " + direction);
        } else {
```java
            // Revert to previous state if move failed
            gameState.undo();
```
            return new MoveResult(false, "Cannot move " + direction);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Processes an Undo action performed by the player.
     *
     * @return {@code false} if there are no steps to undo.
     */
    public boolean processUndo() {
        if (gameState.canUndo()) {
            gameState.undo();
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }
}
